bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the ucl_lex_json_string function where, if a string ends with a '\', the function attempts to read the next character before performing a bounds check, leading to a potential out-of-bounds read.
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable libucl revision `71f16a847414eb6d9b014bdae2844c8a1134fc04`, `ucl_parser_add_chunk_full()` turns the exact 2-byte witness `22 5c` into a `ucl_chunk` whose `end` pointer is `begin + 2`. `ucl_parse_key()` sees the opening quote and routes the remaining single-byte body into `ucl_lex_json_string()`. That scanner reads the final backslash under `while (p < chunk->end)`, enters the escape branch, advances `p` to `chunk->end` with `ucl_chunk_skipc()`, and then immediately executes `c = *p` before checking `if (p >= chunk->end)`. The dereference reads 1 byte 0 bytes past the 2-byte heap testcase buffer, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ` in `ucl_lex_json_string -> ucl_parse_key -> ucl_state_machine`. The fix reorders the dereference so the end-of-chunk check runs first.

source.description: First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled testcase into parser chunk state. It stores the buffer start in `chunk->begin`, seeds `chunk->pos` at the first byte, and derives the exclusive upper bound `chunk->end = begin + len` used by the later bounds checks.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness calls `ucl_parser_add_string(parser, (char *)data, size)` with the exact 2-byte `poc` file `22 5c`; here `len == 2`, so `chunk->end` is one byte past the trailing backslash.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the escape branch has already advanced `p` to `chunk->end`, `c = *p` dereferences the first byte past the 2-byte testcase buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` at `src/ucl_parser.c:1036`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 2-byte region `[0x6020000000b0,0x6020000000b2)`.

root_cause.description: Late bounds check. In the escape branch, the code dereferences `p` before testing `if (p >= chunk->end)`. When the input ends with a lone backslash, `ucl_chunk_skipc()` makes `p == chunk->end`, so this read goes out of bounds. The fix moves the guard before `c = *p`.
root_cause.note: The patch hunk in `patch.diff` removes `c = *p;` above the guard and re-adds it below the `if (p >= chunk->end)` check.

tainted_value_origin.description: The crash-relevant attacker byte is the second and final input byte `0x5c` (`\`). This in-bounds read loads it into `c`, and that value selects the escape-handling branch that advances `p` to the exclusive end pointer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Exact `poc` bytes `22 5c`; after the opening quote is consumed, the remaining byte seen by `ucl_lex_json_string()` is the trailing backslash.

parser_admitted.description: The key parser accepts the first byte of the 2-byte witness as a JSON-style quoted key opener, sets `got_quote`, and continues into `ucl_lex_json_string()` instead of rejecting the input as an invalid identifier.

fine_trace.note: Source. The project parser materializes the attacker-controlled 2-byte testcase as a `ucl_chunk`. For the staged witness `22 5c`, `chunk->pos` starts at the opening quote and `chunk->end` is the exclusive bound immediately after the trailing backslash.

The first byte is `"`, so key parsing takes the quoted-key path. `ucl_chunk_skipc()` consumes that opening quote and updates `p` and `chunk->pos` to the second byte, leaving the trailing backslash as the entire remaining key body.

At entry to `ucl_lex_json_string()`, local `p` is initialized from `chunk->pos`, which step 2 left on the second byte. The loop guard `p < chunk->end` still holds, so this read is in bounds and loads the final byte `0x5c` (`\`) into `c`.

Because `c == '\'`, the escape branch consumes the backslash. `ucl_chunk_skipc()` increments both `p` and `chunk->pos` from offset 1 to offset 2, so `p == chunk->end` and no in-bounds character remains.

Sink and root cause. The code dereferences `p` immediately after step 4, before the following `if (p >= chunk->end)` can report `unfinished escape character`. With `p == chunk->end`, this reads 1 byte 0 bytes past the 2-byte testcase allocation, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/ucl_parser.c:1036`.

depends_on.via: p >= chunk->end not checked before c = *p

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read happened immediately past the 2-byte heap buffer that libFuzzer allocated for the testcase contents.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fix hunk moves `c = *p;` below `if (p >= chunk->end)` in the `c == '\'` escape branch.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, and patch.diff

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_21578 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `gt_results/arvo_21578/poc` to `ucl_add_string_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `ucl_lex_json_string` with stack `ucl_parse_key -> ucl_state_machine`.

format.name: UCL/JSON-style key fragment
format.contract: Exact 2-byte witness `22 5c`: an opening double quote followed immediately by a trailing backslash, with no closing quote and no byte after the backslash. The first byte makes `ucl_parse_key()` enter quoted-key parsing, and the second byte being a lone escape introducer makes `ucl_lex_json_string()` advance `p` to `chunk->end` before the buggy `c = *p` lookahead.
